title: JSON and interface contracts

prerequisite.prompt: Why is reading text different from validating it?
prerequisite.answer: Reading obtains characters; validation checks whether their meaning and values satisfy rules.

vocabulary: A text format for structured values
Converting formatted text into program values
The agreed way one part of a system exchanges data with another
Specified inputs, outputs and error behavior

blocks.text: A fictional activity service supplies JSON text. The input contract is a JSON object with name text and minutes an integer from 0 through 60. The output contract will be a record with accepted and minutes fields. Parsing valid JSON is only the first step.

blocks.title: Python 3 code
blocks.text:
import json
text = '{"name": "Sketch", "minutes": 12}'
record = json.loads(text)
valid = (type(record) is dict
         and type(record.get("name")) is str
         and len(record["name"]) > 0
         and type(record.get("minutes")) is int
         and 0 <= record["minutes"] <= 60)
result = {"accepted": valid, "minutes": record.get("minutes")}
print(json.dumps(result))

blocks.title: Follow the evidence
blocks.caption: Read each row from left to right and connect the evidence to the stated rule.

blocks.text: The output is {"accepted": true, "minutes": 12}. JSON uses lowercase true, false and null; Python uses True, False and None. json.loads converts between representations. The worked output line assumes the parsed top-level value is a dictionary; a robust interface must reject other top-level types before accessing fields.

blocks.label: JSON text contains {"name": "Sketch", "minutes": "12"}. Does parsing fail, or does validation fail?

blocks.text: Single quotes around property names are not valid JSON syntax. Use double quotes in the JSON text. If the whole parsed value is a list, do not call .get on it: check the top-level type first and report a schema failure.
An interface should state what happens for malformed text, wrong structure and invalid values. Do not expose raw private input in error messages. Use only the fictional records supplied for practice.

blocks.label: A JSON record parses successfully. Does that prove its observation is correct?

workbook.title: Translate a value
workbook.prompt: What Python value does JSON null become? What JSON value represents Python True?

workbook.title: Separate failures
workbook.prompt: Classify {"minutes": "5"} and {minutes: 5} as valid JSON text or malformed JSON.
workbook.answer: The first is valid JSON but its minutes field fails the integer schema. The second is malformed because the key is not double-quoted.

workbook.title: Repair the interface
workbook.prompt: A parser accepts a JSON list then crashes on .get. What check belongs before field access?
workbook.answer: Require type(record) is dict and handle failure before any .get or keyed field access.

workbook.title: Specify independently
workbook.prompt: Define a JSON contract for {"label": "Box", "count": 4}: nonempty text label, integer count 0 through 10. Give a valid case, a wrong-type case and a missing-field case with expected acceptance.
workbook.answer: Valid Box/4 accepted; count "4" rejected for type; absent count rejected as missing. State that malformed JSON and non-object top levels are also rejected.

workbook.title: Limit parsing
workbook.prompt: A JSON record parses successfully. Does that prove its observation is correct?
workbook.answer: No. Syntax, schema validity and observational truth are separate checks.

teacher.background: Teach Week 26 as a two-session investigation using fictional data. A fictional activity service supplies JSON text. The input contract is a JSON object with name text and minutes an integer from 0 through 60. The output contract will be a record with accepted and minutes fields. Parsing valid JSON is only the first step. Assess the three stated outcomes through the independent task, not by copying the worked result.

Use W3 to diagnose and repair the stated failure; rerun an earlier case.
Collect W4 independently, including code or plan, predictions and explanations, before hints.
Discuss W5 and the exit; use the fresh retry when support was needed.
teacher.guidedAnswer: Parsing succeeds; validation fails because minutes is text. Exit: No. Syntax, schema validity and observational truth are separate checks.
